newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. go-it-alone strike was wrong, Mandela says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. go-it-alone strike was wrong, Mandela says.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Friday condemned the United States for its unilateral attack on Iraq but blamed Baghdad for triggering the crisis.
"While I condemn the action taken by the United States of America, I also condemn the action taken by Iraq," Mandela told reporters during a photo opportunity in a township near Johannesburg.
He said international law prohibited the sort of military retribution ordered by U.S. President Bill Clinton this week after Iraq's armed incursion into Kurdish northern Iraq.
"Any action that has to be taken of this nature must be taken by the United Nations and not an individual country," Mandela said.
But he stressed his criticism of the U.S. did not mean his government agreed with the actions of Iraq: "We also condemn their action."
